1.why: Reset tokens are stored with accountId and update-password requires record.accountId === account.id plus session claim checks.

2.why: A reset record is bound to one accountId and claimedBy session, so the same code cannot be used by a different user/session.

3.why: update-password marks the reset used but never clears authenticatedAccountId on other existing sessions, so prior logins remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS is set, and cookies use the Secure flag.

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes; in-memory user fields like email are not encrypted.

6.why: No real email body includes profile data; responses use a generic eligibility message without exposing account details.

7.why: Inputs are type/length/format validated (validEmail/validPassword/bodyOf) and user values are applied via textContent/JSON, not raw HTML.

8.why: Client reset links are built only as location.origin + '/reset?token=...' with no user-controlled redirect target.

9.why: There is no user-controlled HTML in any mail path; simulated delivery only logs server-generated tokens.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but reset/MFA tokens are returned as mock fields and written into the on-page logs panel.

11.why: Initial plaintext password and the fixed MFA secret '246810' are hardcoded in source despite bcrypt for the stored password hash.

12.why: The single built-in demo account (helena@hospital.test / Initial!Passw0rd2025) is accepted with no default-credential ban.

13.why: limited() throttles reset, verify, MFA, and login attempts, and failedLogins lock the account after repeated failures.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same message and a mockToken; login failures use one generic 401 message.

15.why: Codes come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, URL-safe), are hashed at rest, and are tied to a specific accountId/session.
